atlas-kw.0086: Kuwaiti workers in the private sector were about 72,800 at the end of June 2024 against about 404,900 in government; by June 2026 the Kuwait Times figures imply about 98,500 in the private sector, a rise driven by the localisation policy. This second step is our reading.
atlas-kw.0088: A university accredited by the higher-education ministry, such as Kuwait University, GUST or AUK, sponsors the visa. Kuwait is not in the Apostille Convention: diplomas and records need full consular legalisation, with wet-ink signatures.
atlas-kw.0089: Paid work off campus is forbidden.
atlas-kw.0090: visa 10 KWD; residence 20 KWD a year; health insurance 100 KWD a year
atlas-kw.0091: Kuwait has no visa for interns. An internship on a tourist, business or visit visa, even unpaid, is illegal work leading to detention and expulsion; only students already resident may do unpaid curricular placements.
atlas-kw.0092: There is no grace period. A graduate with a formal offer before the student residence is cancelled can move straight to a private-sector work residence; otherwise you must leave.
atlas-kw.0094: The employer obtains the work permit and entry visa; within 60 days of arrival come the medical, fingerprints, residence and Civil ID. The employer pays all first-year fees by law.
atlas-kw.0095: Engineers need degree equivalency from the higher-education ministry, doctors the Kuwait licensing exam; enter with a downgraded job title and it cannot be corrected later.
atlas-kw.0097: You cannot move to a new employer in the first three years without the current sponsor’s written consent.
atlas-kw.0099: Unpaid archive work, interviews or seminars up to 90 days can be done on a tourist eVisa; structured research at KISR or Kuwait University needs a visit visa from the host, and paid research beyond 90 days a government contract. PhD students are students; KFAS or KISR funding makes them employees.
atlas-kw.0100: Kuwait has no working-holiday agreements; working, even remotely for foreign clients, on a tourist visa leads to arrest and expulsion.
atlas-kw.0102: EU and UK citizens get an eVisa or visa on arrival for up to 90 days, with no work. A visit visa can become residence only exceptionally, with a 150 KWD surcharge.
atlas-kw.0105: Kuwait is not in the apostille convention: have your criminal record (under 3 months old) translated into Arabic and fully legalised at the Kuwaiti consulate in Milan or embassy in Rome (€25 a stamp), then countersigned by the Foreign Ministry in Kuwait (5 KWD a document).
atlas-kw.0106: Since an inactive lung scar counts as unfit, a high-resolution chest X-ray at home before you resign or pay for the move is a prudent check.
atlas-kw.0107: Entering on the work entry visa starts a 60-day deadline to complete residence. You may not start work, even informally, before the Civil ID or its digital version is issued.
atlas-kw.0108: A positive or doubtful result in the medical screening, including healed tuberculosis scars, means deportation and a lifetime ban from all Gulf states.
atlas-kw.0109: Register with the civil information authority (PACI) for the Civil ID: the digital ID appears at once in the Hawiti app, and the chip card costs 5.250 KWD.
atlas-kw.0110: After arriving, have the compulsory medical screening at the Ministry of Health centres in Shuwaikh or Sabhan, and pay the state health insurance (100 KWD a year, or 130 KWD through Dhaman); for workers the employer pays.
atlas-kw.0111: The Central Bank has frozen the cards and accounts of anyone who did not complete the biometric registration with the Interior Ministry; salaries are paid through the Wages Protection System.
atlas-kw.0112: Any old scar or calcification on the chest X-ray is treated as TB: medically unfit, deportation and a lifelong Gulf ban, with no appeal. Get a chest X-ray at home first.
atlas-kw.0113: An employer can file an “absence” report: the Civil ID is revoked, accounts frozen and a travel ban imposed.
atlas-kw.0114: Overstaying a visit visa costs 10 KWD a day and a permanent ban.
atlas-kw.0115: Using a degree the ministry has not recognised is a crime carrying up to five years in prison.
